headline.headline: SPROAT BEANS THREE BREWERS, PIRATES TAKE GAME ONE 7-6 IN WILD SATURDAY OPENER
headline.deck: Pittsburgh starter hits Mangum, Reynolds and O'Hearn as Pirates claw past Milwaukee in doubleheader sweep
headline.body:
PITTSBURGH — Thomas Sproat earned the win Saturday afternoon in one of the stranger pitching lines of the 2026 season, hitting three Milwaukee Brewers batters — Mangum, Bryan Reynolds and Ryan O'Hearn — while guiding Pittsburgh to a 7-6 victory in the first game of a doubleheader at PNC Park. The Pirates staked an early claim, scoring two runs in the first inning, surrendered the lead through five when Milwaukee erupted for three in the fifth to go up 5-3, then reclaimed control with a four-run seventh that proved the decisive blow.

The Brewers managed six runs but could not hold back a Pittsburgh lineup that kept finding answers late. The 22,484 fans in attendance watched the lead change hands across a 2-hour, 49-minute contest that swung sharply in the seventh inning when the Pirates posted four runs to break a tight game open and hand Sproat the victory despite his unusual contribution to the hit-by-pitch ledger.

Game two proved nearly as gripping, with Pittsburgh winning 3-2 behind a shutout ninth to complete the sweep. Milwaukee, leaders of the NL Central entering the day, absorbed back-to-back losses that tighten the division race heading into the All-Star break. The Brewers were held scoreless in seven of nine innings in the nightcap, with O'Hearn hit by a Drohan pitch and Christian Yelich plunked by Ramírez, underscoring a rough afternoon at the plate and on the basepaths for Milwaukee.

secondary.headline: WICKENHEISER OUT AS MAPLE LEAFS PURGE FRONT OFFICE
secondary.deck: Hockey legend and assistant GM among several executives dismissed in sweeping Toronto overhaul
secondary.body:
TORONTO — Hayley Wickenheiser, one of the most decorated players in the history of women's hockey and the Toronto Maple Leafs' assistant general manager, was fired Saturday as part of a wide-ranging front office purge that signals a dramatic reshaping of the organization. Wickenheiser had been seen as a rising voice in NHL management since joining the Leafs' executive ranks, and her dismissal drew immediate reaction across the league.

The firings come during the NHL's second round of playoffs and with free agency already reshaping rosters across the league. The scope of the Toronto housecleaning suggests ownership has lost confidence in the current hockey operations structure after yet another postseason disappointment. The Leafs, long criticized for failing to advance deep into the playoffs despite perennial regular-season contention, appear determined to rebuild the decision-making apparatus from the top down.

secondary.headline: KHOSLA GROUP AGREES TO BUY SEATTLE SEAHAWKS FOR $9.6 BILLION
secondary.deck: Niners limited partner Vinod Khosla leads group set to acquire franchise in record-setting NFL sale
secondary.body:
SEATTLE — A group led by Silicon Valley investor and San Francisco 49ers limited partner Vinod Khosla has agreed to purchase the Seattle Seahawks, with sources telling reporters the sale price sits at approximately $9.6 billion, a figure that would rank among the largest in professional sports franchise history. The deal signals another seismic shift in NFL ownership as league valuations continue to climb to staggering heights.

The Seahawks have been one of the NFC's cornerstone franchises for more than two decades, winning Super Bowl XLVIII and making consistent playoff appearances. It remains unclear what changes in football operations, if any, the Khosla group intends to pursue, though transitions of this magnitude at the ownership level often precede broader organizational reviews. The sale requires approval from NFL owners before it becomes official.

secondary.headline: GIANTS RALLY IN SIXTH TO DOWN ROCKIES, 4-2, AT PACKED ORACLE PARK
secondary.deck: San Francisco erupts for three sixth-inning runs, and Karros hits his ninth homer in victory over Colorado
secondary.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — The San Francisco Giants trailed the Colorado Rockies 1-0 through five innings Saturday before erupting for three runs in the sixth to take command and win 4-2 in front of 35,190 fans at Oracle Park. A solo run in the fifth drew San Francisco even, and the three-run sixth proved more than enough against a Rockies club that managed lone runs in the third and eighth but could not sustain any offense.

The big individual moment came from Karros, who clubbed his ninth home run of the season to add to San Francisco's total. Colorado's Tovar struck out as a pinch hitter in the ninth, and Sullivan also grounded out late in the game as the Rockies ran out of answers against the Giants' pitching staff. The win gives San Francisco a strong result heading into the second half of the season, bolstered by 35,000-plus in the seats on a Saturday afternoon in the Bay Area.

column.headline: SPROAT'S HIT BATTERS TELL THE STORY: PITTSBURGH IS PLAYING WITH AN EDGE
column.body:
Thomas Sproat hit three batters Saturday and still walked off PNC Park with a win. That sentence alone tells you something about the Pittsburgh Pirates in July 2026. This is not a team playing careful baseball. This is a team scrapping for every inch of the NL Central race, willing to absorb the chaos that comes with a pitcher drilling Mangum, Reynolds and O'Hearn in the same afternoon, so long as the seven runs hold up in the final inning. They did. They usually do for teams playing with this kind of stubborn momentum.

Meanwhile, Milwaukee took two losses Saturday that should alarm the Brewers faithful far more than a single bad series. The NL Central leaders absorbed the sweep without ever truly solving Pittsburgh's pitching in the nightcap, getting blanked in seven of nine innings in game two. The All-Star break arrives soon, and the Brewers will spend it knowing the Pirates are coming. That is not a comfortable place for a division leader to spend the summer.

story.headline: PIRATES SWEEP BREWERS WITH BACK-TO-BACK WINS, DEAL NL CENTRAL LEADERS A DOUBLE BLOW
story.deck: Pittsburgh takes both ends of Saturday twin bill, eyes series sweep Sunday
story.body:
PITTSBURGH, July 12 -- The Pittsburgh Pirates did something Saturday that few teams have managed against the Milwaukee Brewers this season, beating the NL Central leaders twice in one afternoon and setting up a potential sweep of the three-game series Sunday at PNC Park. Pittsburgh took the opener 7-6 in a slugfest, then closed out the nightcap 3-2 in a tighter affair, dropping Milwaukee to 59-37 while the surging Pirates climbed to 49-47.

The afternoon game was anything but tidy. Pittsburgh starter Sproat earned the win despite hitting three batters, including Mangum, Bryan Reynolds and O'Hearn, while Pittsburgh built an early 3-0 lead through three innings only to watch Milwaukee storm back with three runs in the fifth to tie it. The Pirates answered with a four-run seventh to put the game away, with Jake Bauers launching his 18th home run of the season. Sal Frelick hit his fourth and Enmanuel Valdez added his ninth for Milwaukee, but the Brewers stranded 15 runners and never could deliver the knockout punch. Pittsburgh left 16 on base themselves before closing it out 7-6.

The nightcap was quieter but no less decisive. Valdez connected for his 10th home run of the season as Pittsburgh scored twice in the fourth and once in the sixth to hold off Milwaukee 3-2. The Brewers stranded a staggering 20 runners across nine innings, going hitless when it mattered most. Pittsburgh now stands one victory away from a sweep of the division leaders Sunday, a result that would further tighten an NL Central race Milwaukee had appeared to have well in hand entering the weekend.

story.headline: PLAYOFF FIELD TAKES SHAPE AS SUMMER SHOWDOWNS HEAT UP ACROSS THE LEAGUE
story.deck: Five marquee matchups signal the NBA's postseason picture is coming into sharp focus.
story.body:
The NBA playoff race roared back to life Sunday as five high-stakes matchups delivered the kind of July fireworks that have come to define the league's expanded summer schedule. The Los Angeles Lakers and Dallas Mavericks headlined the afternoon slate, with LeBron James and Luka Doncic renewing their rivalry in a contest that carried genuine Western Conference seeding implications. Meanwhile, the Houston Rockets and Toronto Raptors battled in a game that could determine which franchise earns the final guaranteed playoff berth in their respective conferences.

In the Eastern Conference, the Atlanta Hawks and Brooklyn Nets squared off in a matchup that pit Trae Young's relentless playmaking against Brooklyn's retooled roster, which has leaned heavily on its young core since last winter's front-office overhaul. Across town in Minneapolis, the Denver Nuggets and Minnesota Timberwolves delivered a physical clash, with Nikola Jokic and Anthony Edwards trading buckets in a rivalry that has smoldered since Denver's title run earlier this decade. The Nuggets' depth and Jokic's floor vision remained the primary difference between two franchises pointed in opposite directions.

The final game of the day, New York against San Antonio, drew the largest crowd reaction from Knicks faithful, who packed Madison Square Garden hoping to watch their squad clinch a favorable playoff seed. Karl-Anthony Towns controlled the interior while the Spurs leaned on Victor Wembanyama's length to contest every New York possession. With the postseason bracket set to crystallize over the next two weeks, Sunday's slate served as a loud reminder that the road to the 2026 NBA championship runs through some of the most competitive basketball the league has produced in years.

story.headline: DUCKS MATCH $90M OFFER SHEET, KEEP CARLSSON; LEAFS FIRE WICKENHEISER IN FRONT OFFICE PURGE
story.deck: Anaheim retains its 21-year-old franchise center at a record $18 million per season.
story.body:
The Anaheim Ducks blinked at the edge of the cliff Sunday, then stepped back. The club matched the Philadelphia Flyers' stunning five-year, $90 million offer sheet for star center Leo Carlsson, locking up the 21-year-old Swede at $18 million annually through the prime of his career in what stands as the richest offer sheet in NHL history. The decision ends a week of white-knuckle suspense that had league executives, agents and fans questioning whether a small-market Ducks franchise would absorb the financial commitment or surrender its most prized asset to a hungry Eastern Conference rival.

Carlsson, the second overall pick in the 2023 draft, spoke publicly about the saga Sunday, describing the offer sheet period as surreal while stopping short of saying he had pushed for a move to Philadelphia. The Flyers swung the historic sheet as a calculated gamble to accelerate their rebuild, dangling a contract figure that forced Anaheim's ownership group to make a franchise-defining call. By matching, the Ducks now carry one of the heaviest center commitments in the Western Conference alongside a young core that includes Mason McTavish, signaling the organization believes its contention window is opening sooner than expected.

Meanwhile, the Toronto Maple Leafs sent shockwaves through the hockey world by firing assistant general manager Hayley Wickenheiser as part of a sweeping front office purge that signals deep organizational unrest on Carlton Street. Wickenheiser, a four-time Olympic gold medalist and one of the most celebrated players in the history of the women's game, had been considered a pillar of the Leafs' front office rebuild since joining the hockey operations staff. The dismissals raise urgent questions about the direction of a franchise that has endured decades of playoff heartbreak and is now, once again, tearing down the people tasked with ending it.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS TEAMS RETOOL FOR 2026 CAMPAIGN
story.deck: Three franchises swap signal-callers in a frantic May that is reshaping the NFC landscape.
story.body:
The phones have not stopped ringing inside NFL front offices since the calendar flipped to May, and the biggest deals have centered on quarterbacks desperate teams could not land during the April draft. The Cleveland Browns sent a second-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders for Gardner Minshew, banking on the veteran's experience to stabilize an offense that cycled through four starters during the 2025 season. Meanwhile, the Carolina Panthers agreed to a two-year, $54 million contract with free agent Jameis Winston, betting the 32-year-old still carries enough arm talent to rebuild a roster that finished 4-13 last year.

The draft class itself continues to generate headlines weeks after Commissioner Roger Goodell called the names in Green Bay. analysts are already debating whether Miami's first-round pick, Texas quarterback Arch Manning, can handle the jump to professional football after a dazzling college career, while the New England Patriots drew praise throughout the league for their selection of Penn State edge rusher Abdul Carter with the fifth overall pick. Patriots head coach Jerod Mayo called Carter a foundational piece, the kind of disruptive talent New England has lacked since Chandler Jones departed years ago.

Training camp storylines are also beginning to take shape nearly two months before rosters report. The San Francisco 49ers must answer questions about Brock Purdy's surgically repaired throwing shoulder after he missed the final six weeks of the 2025 season, and the Dallas Cowboys are navigating a contract standoff with wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, whose holdout threat has rattled an already restless fanbase. League sources indicated Friday that Lamb's representatives and Cowboys ownership exchanged new figures this week, suggesting a resolution could arrive before mandatory minicamp opens in June.
